newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Basque gvt to issue 20 bln pesetas 5-y bond.
newsitem.headline: Spain Basque gvt to issue 20 bln pesetas 5-y bond.

text.p: Spain's Basque regional government said on Friday it will issue on May 14 five-year bonds worth 20 billion pesetaswith an annual coupon of 5.40 percent.
The bonds will yield eight basis points above the 7.90 percent February 2002 Spanish Treasury bond, the regional government said in a statement.
The maturity date will be May 14, 2002, while pay date is May 14 1997.
The following banks are participating in the issue: Banco de Negocios de Argentaria, Bilbao Bizkaia Kutxa, Caja Vital Kutxa and Gipuzkoa Donostia Kutxa.
A regional official said it is the first issuance of the year. The Basque region issued 63 billion pesetas in bonds during 1996 in three separate offers.
For 1997, the Basque regional government has a maximum allowed issuance of 38.96 billion pesetas.
These bonds are mainly sold to domestic investors because of the regional tax system.
For historic reasons, the Basque country collects all taxes in the region and, unlike other regions, does not return a 25 percent withholding tax to foreign investors.
This reduces interest from potential foreign buyers.
The Basque region has the same credit rating as the Kingdom of Spain -- AA by Standard and Poor's and Aa2 by Moody's.
